I need to clarify what is meant by "Malta Memorial," as it could refer to several sites. It’s likely the Commonwealth Air Forces memorial in Floriana, which commemorates airmen missing in the Mediterranean. The **Malta Memorial** usually refers to the **Commonwealth Air Forces Memorial in Floriana, Malta**, a major **Commonwealth War Graves Commission (CWGC)** memorial.

## What it is
It commemorates **airmen of the Commonwealth air forces** who **died in the Second World War** during operations connected with the **Mediterranean theatre**, and who **have no known grave**.

## Who is commemorated
It honours members of the:
- **Royal Air Force (RAF)**
- **Royal Canadian Air Force (RCAF)**
- **Royal Australian Air Force (RAAF)**
- **Royal New Zealand Air Force (RNZAF)**
- **South African Air Force (SAAF)**

and other Commonwealth air personnel lost in the region.

The memorial bears the names of **more than 2,000 missing airmen**. The commonly cited figure is **2,298**.

## Location
It stands in **Floriana**, just outside **Valletta**, Malta, in an elevated and prominent position overlooking the island’s Grand Harbour area.

## Why Malta
Malta was one of the most important Allied bases in the Mediterranean during the Second World War. From Malta, Allied aircraft:
- attacked Axis shipping
- escorted convoys
- carried out reconnaissance
- supported operations in **North Africa**, **Sicily**, **Italy**, and across the Mediterranean

Because air combat and maritime patrols over the Mediterranean often ended with aircraft lost at sea, many of the dead had **no recoverable remains**, which is why a memorial to the missing was needed.

## Historical context
The memorial reflects Malta’s central wartime role:
- Malta endured intense **Axis bombing**
- it was strategically vital for control of Mediterranean supply routes
- RAF and Commonwealth aircrew operating from Malta faced especially high casualty rates

The men named there include those lost in:
- bomber missions
- fighter operations
- anti-shipping strikes
- transport flights
- reconnaissance patrols
- air-sea operations over the Mediterranean

## Design
The memorial was designed in a formal monumental style typical of postwar CWGC memorial architecture. It consists of a **large stone structure with inscribed panels** listing the names of the missing.

It was designed by **Sir Edward Maufe**, a noted British architect who also designed other CWGC memorials.

The sculpture on the memorial is by **Vernon Hill**.

## Unveiling
The Malta Memorial was **unveiled in 1954**.

## Administration
It is maintained by the **Commonwealth War Graves Commission**.

## Significance
The memorial is significant because it:
- commemorates those with **no known grave**
- reflects the air war over the Mediterranean
- symbolizes Malta’s wartime importance
- serves as a place of remembrance for families whose relatives were never recovered

## Related remembrance in Malta
Malta has several other major war memorial and CWGC sites, so people sometimes confuse them with the Malta Memorial. These include:
- **Naval Memorials and cemeteries**
- **Capuccini Naval Cemetery**
- **Pembroke Military Cemetery**
- various siege and wartime monuments in Valletta and Floriana

So if someone says “Malta Memorial,” they usually mean the **CWGC air forces memorial to the missing**, not every wartime monument on the island.

## If you want to visit
A visitor can generally expect:
- a formal stone monument
- inscribed names
- a quiet commemorative setting
- views over Floriana/Valletta surroundings

If you want, I can also give you:
1. a **full historical background of the Malta Memorial**,  
2. a **description of specific names or units commemorated there**, or  
3. a **comparison with other CWGC memorials in Malta**.
